translations.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the command of God our Savior and of the Lord Jesus Christ, our hope,
to Timothy, my true son in the faith: grace, mercy, and peace from God our Father and from Christ Jesus our Lord.
As I urged you to stay on in Ephesus when I was going to Macedonia, so that you might instruct certain people not to teach anything different,
and not to pay attention to Jewish fables and endless genealogies, which bring about disputes rather than God's stewardship, which is by faith.
But the goal of the commandment is love from a pure heart and a good conscience and a sincere faith,
which some have failed to reach, and they have turned aside to empty talk.
They want to be teachers of the law, yet they understand neither what they are saying nor the things about which they make confident claims.
But we know that the law is good, if one uses it properly;

knowing this, that the law is not laid down for the righteous, but for the lawless and the disobedient, the ungodly and sinners, the unholy and the profane, those who abuse their fathers and those who abuse their mothers, murderers,
fornicators, sodomites, slave-dealers, liars, perjurers, and whatever else is contrary to the teaching of this life,
according to the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, which was entrusted to me. (2)
And I am thankful to him who strengthened me, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he judged me faithful and appointed me to this ministry,
though formerly I was a blasphemer and a persecutor and an insolent man; but I was shown mercy, because I acted in ignorance¹ in unbelief.
And the grace of our Lord overflowed all the more, together with faith and love in Christ Jesus.
The saying is trustworthy and worthy of full acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the first.
But for this reason I was shown mercy, so that in me first Jesus Christ might display all his patience, as an example to those who would afterwards believe in him for eternal life.
Now to the King of the ages, incorruptible, invisible, the only wise God, be honor and glory for ever and ever. Amen. (3)
This commandment I entrust to you, my son Timothy, in keeping with the prophecies previously made about you, so that by them you may wage the good warfare,
holding faith and a good conscience, which some have rejected and so have made shipwreck of their faith;
among them are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have handed over to the devil, so that they may be taught not to blaspheme.
First of all, then, I urge that supplications, prayers, worship, and thanksgivings be made for all people,
for kings and all who are in authority, so that we may live in peace and quiet in all godliness and holiness,
for this is good and pleasing before God our Savior,
who wills all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
For there is one God, and one mediator between God and humankind, the man Jesus Christ,
who gave himself as a ransom for all, as a testimony in his own times,
for which I have been appointed a preacher and an apostle — I speak the truth in Christ and do not lie — a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
So I desire that men pray in every place, lifting up holy hands, without anger and scheming of the heart;
likewise that women adorn themselves with the ornament of orderliness, modestly and with dignity, not with braided hair, or gold, or pearls, or very costly clothing,
but with what is becoming to women who profess the service of God through good works.
Let a woman learn in silence with all submission.
I do not command women to teach, nor to rule over a husband, but rather that she be in quietness.
For Adam was created first, then Eve.
And Adam was not deceived, but the woman was deceived and transgressed the law.
But she will be saved through childbearing, if they remain in faith and love and holiness, with dignity.
The saying is trustworthy: if anyone desires the office of bishop, his heart is set on a good work.
A bishop must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, pure, orderly, hospitable, learned,
not a drinker of wine, not greedy [?], not one who acquires shameful gain, but gentle, not quarrelsome [?], not a lover of silver,
one who manages his own household well and keeps his children in submission with all dignity.
But if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how will he labor for the churches of God?
He must not be a new convert, so that he does not become puffed up and fall into the condemnation of the devil.
But he must also have a good testimony from those around him, so that he may not fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.
Deacons likewise must be pure, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not seekers of shameful gain,
Let them hold the mystery of the faith with a pure mind.
And let these also be tested first, and only then let them serve as deacons, if they are blameless.
Likewise let their wives be dignified, not slanderers, but vigilant, faithful in all things.
Let deacons be husbands of one wife, managing well their children and their own households.
For those who serve well as deacons acquire good honor for themselves and great openness in the faith of Christ Jesus.
I write this to you, and I hope to come to you soon;
But if I delay, it is so that you may know how one must walk in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and firm foundation of the truth.

And, as is confessed, great is the mystery of godliness: God was revealed in the flesh and justified in the Spirit, appeared to angels, was preached among the Gentiles, was believed in by the world, and was exalted in glory.
But the Holy Spirit says plainly that in the last times some will depart from the faith and will give heed to those deceiving spirits and to the teaching of demons,
through hypocrisy and words of falsehood, seared in their own mind,
they will forbid marriage and keep people away from foods, which God created to be received with thanksgiving by believers and by those who know the truth.
For every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected if it is received with thanksgiving,
for it is sanctified by the word of God and by prayer.
Teach this to the brothers, and you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished by the words of the faith and of the good teaching that you have followed.
But abstain from those defiled and old-womanish fables. And train yourself in godliness.
For bodily training is of profit for a short time; but the service of God is profitable in every way, for it holds the promise of life, both the present and the one to come.
This saying is trustworthy and worthy of full acceptance.
For this is why we toil and suffer reproach: we hope in the living God, who is the Savior of all people, and especially of those who believe.
Command these things and teach them.
Let no one despise your youth; but be an example to the believers in word, in conduct, in love, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
Until I come, give your attention to reading, to encouragement, and to teaching.
Do not neglect the grace that is with you, which was given to you through prophecy, with the laying on of hands of the priesthood.
Practise these things and devote yourself to them, so that your progress may be evident to everyone.
Take heed to yourself and to teaching, and persist in these things; for by doing this you will save both yourself and those who obey you.
Do not be angry with an old man, but entreat him as a father; treat young men as brothers,
old women as mothers, young women as sisters, in all purity. [Section] 11
Honour widows who are truly widows.
If any widow has children or grandchildren, let them learn first to show piety toward their own household and to honor their parents, for this is good and pleasing before God.
But the true widow, left all alone, hopes in the Lord and persists in supplication and prayer night and day.
But she who lives for pleasure is dead even while she lives.
Command these things too, so that they may be blameless.
But if anyone does not take care of his own, and especially of his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
Let no one be enrolled as a widow who is less than sixty years old, who has been the wife of one husband,

and is attested in good works: if she has brought up children, if she has shown hospitality to guests, if she has washed the feet of the saints, if she has helped the afflicted, if she has devoted herself to every good work.
But keep away from young widows, for when those women of Christ grow wanton, they desire to marry.
They are under judgment, because they have set aside their first faith.
And along with that they learn idleness and going about from house to house, and not only idleness, but also gossip and prying, and they say what is improper.
I therefore want young women to marry, to bear children, to manage a household, and to give the adversary no occasion for reproach.
For some have already turned aside to follow the devil.
If any believer has widows, let that person provide for them, and let the church not be burdened, so that it may provide for the other widows. [Section] 12
Let the elders who rule well be counted worthy of double honor, especially those who labor zealously in the word and in teaching.
For the scripture says: You shall not muzzle the threshing ox; and: The laborer is worthy of his wages.
Do not accept an accusation against a priest, except on the evidence of two or three witnesses.
And those who sin, rebuke before everyone, so that the others may be afraid.
I testify before God and Jesus Christ and the chosen angels that you are to keep these things without double-mindedness; do nothing out of partiality.
Do not lay hands on anyone hastily, nor share in the sins of another; keep yourself pure.
Do not drink only water, but also use a little wine for your stomach and for your frequent infirmity.
The sins of some men are evident beforehand and go ahead of them to judgment; those of others follow after them.
Likewise good works are evident beforehand; and if anyone has them otherwise, they cannot be hidden.
As many as are under the yoke of slavery, let them regard their own masters as worthy of all honor, so that the name of God and this teaching may not be blasphemed.

Let those who have believing masters not despise them because they are brothers. Instead, let them serve them all the more, because they are believers and beloved, partners in the good work. Teach and urge these things.
If anyone teaches otherwise and does not come to the life-giving teachings of our Lord Jesus Christ and to the teaching of this godliness,
he is puffed up and knows nothing. Rather, he is sick with disputing and with quarrels over words, from which come envy, strife, blasphemies, evil suspicions,
anger, the thinking of corrupted people who are lacking in the truth, who suppose that godliness is a means of gain. Withdraw from such people.
But godliness with contentment is in truth great gain.
For we brought nothing into the world; it is evident that neither are we able to carry anything out.
But if we have food and covering for the body, let us be content with these.
But those who want riches fall into temptation and a snare and into many senseless and harmful desires, which sink people into destruction and perdition.
For the love of money is the root of all evils; some, desiring it, have strayed from the faith and have pierced themselves with many pains.
But you, man of God, flee from this and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, gentleness.
Fight the good fight of faith; take hold of the eternal life to which you were called, and you confessed the good confession before many witnesses.
I charge you before God, who gives life to all things, and before Christ Jesus, who testified the good confession under Pontius Pilate,
to keep the commandment spotless and blameless until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ,
which he will show in his own times, the blessed and only mighty one, the King of kings and Lord of lords,
who alone has immortality and dwells in unapproachable light, whom no human being has seen or is able to see, to whom belong honor and eternal power. Amen.
Command those who are rich in this world not to be haughty, nor to hope in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who gives us everything richly for enjoyment,
and to do good, to be rich in good works, to be generous givers, to share with others,
and to store up for themselves a good foundation for the time to come, so that they may hold fast to eternal life.
O Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you, and turn away from the foul, empty utterances and the contradictions of what is falsely called knowledge,
which some have professed, and they have fallen away empty from the faith. Grace be with you. Amen.
